previous_notes.author: Dr. R. Visser (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with a PSA of 3.5 ng/mL. Digital rectal examination was normal. Discussed the mildly elevated PSA and decided to repeat the PSA in 6 months. Referred for baseline MRI.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. Visser (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient returned for follow-up. PSA measured at 3.4 ng/mL, stable compared to previous value. Discussed the results and the decision to proceed with a prostate biopsy. Biopsy was scheduled and performed. Pathology results showed Gleason 3+3, ISUP grade group 1. Discussed the findings and the option of active surveillance. Patient expressed interest in understanding the long-term implications.

pathology_report:
Biopsy timepoint 1: Prostate biopsy performed. Histological examination reveals adenocarcinoma of the prostate with a Gleason score of 3+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 1. The growth pattern is acinar. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified.

Biopsy timepoint 2 (latest): Prostate biopsy performed. Histological examination reveals adenocarcinoma of the prostate with a Gleason score of 3+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 1. The growth pattern is acinar. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified.

Summary: The histological grade has remained stable across both biopsy timepoints, with persistent ISUP grade group 1 disease.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 4.
